passages.note: House Third Reading roll call naming him as a Y; the page prints no operative text.

passages.provision_quote: On receipt of a report of the existence of a homeless encampment, a city or town shall notify the owner to remove the owner's tent, structure or other personal property from the area in which the encampment is located.
passages.note: Bill text: mandatory notice and clearance, with criminal liability limited to encampments on private property and to drug use; no civil penalty is created.
Bill overview: sponsors are Wadsack and Jones, not this person; it carries the House tally and the veto.

rows.reasoning: His only act here is a Y on final passage of SB 1413 (2023), a single-subject bill that orders a city, town or county to notify an encampment owner and then claim and dispose of the property after twenty-four hours. That mandatory clearance matches the first clause of the rung that would be "Prohibiting encampments on public property", but the bill creates no civil penalty and only a single notice, so "enforced through graduated warnings and civil penalties" is unevidenced; its criminal exposure reaches only encampments on private property and drug offenses, so the rung reading "Banning public camping and sleeping with criminal penalties to maintain public safety and order" is not established either.
